$comment: An example nudge.json. Copy it to nudge.json and keep what you need; `nudge doctor` checks it. Keys named $comment are ignored.

assistants.$comment: name is URL-safe and picks the assistant in -a and /v1/a/<name>. database is relative to this file (default data/<name>.sqlite). Without a model, Anthropic's claude-sonnet-5 is used; it reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
assistants.name: robin
assistants.instructions: Answer in the language you are written to. Keep answers short.

budget.$comment: Monthly limits on model spend in USD. Past perPlayerUsd a player's messages are refused; past monthlyUsd nothing goes to the model until the month ends. warnAt is the share at which people are told. `nudge usage` shows the spend.

extensions.$comment: from is a file or package directory relative to this file, or an installed package name. settings are checked against the extension's own schema. rooms lists the kinds of room it is on in by default (lobby, personal, shared; default all); people can turn it on or off per room with /extensions. Set enabled to false to keep an entry without installing it.
Optional: finds people's names and street addresses the regular detectors miss, with name lists and rules on the host. extraNames adds your own.
Receipts and other documents per room: uploaded on the room's Documents page, text read on the host, files stored encrypted.
Shared lists per room (shopping, packing), for the model and on the room's Lists page.
Watches: the assistant checks something on a schedule with its tools and tells the room only what is new. Each check is a model run, so minMinutes caps how often.
Web search through your own SearXNG (JSON output on), and reading a page as text.
Talk to the assistant from Telegram. The bot token comes from TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; people link with /link <code from nudge pair>. Off here (enabled: false) so the example works without a token.
Talk to the assistant from Signal through `signal-cli -a <number> daemon --tcp --receive-mode=on-connection` on this host.
Talk to the assistant from Matrix rooms without end-to-end encryption, as a bot account whose access token is in MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN.

assistants.$comment: A second assistant with its own database, on the local server below. Its rooms, players and memory are separate from robin's.
assistants.name: pocket

providers.$comment: Any OpenAI-compatible server, such as llama-server, Ollama or vLLM. apiKeyEnv names the environment variable holding its key; leave it out for keyless servers. Most local servers reject the developer role.

backup.$comment: Encrypted backups nudge serve makes on its own: everything needed to restore, into dir (relative to this file). The key is NUDGE_BACKUP_KEY or nudge-backup.key beside this file; keep a copy of it off the machine. nudge backup makes one now, nudge restore <file> --to <dir> unpacks one.

push.$comment: Browser notifications from nudge serve. preview: "room" (the default) names only the room; "text" adds the start of the message. subject: how push services reach you, a mailto: or https: address; default the --public-url when it is HTTPS.
push.subject: mailto:you@example.com
